text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000215's 99215 rate is elevated in every complexity tier, including low-complexity patients, but only three documented 99215 claims are available, too few to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern points away from a sicker panel. The excess 99215 share holds after risk adjustment and appears in every complexity tier. It is starkest on patients with 0 or 1 conditions, such as C0119754 (age 21, hyperlipidemia only) and C0119814 (age 24, obesity only). The documentation is too thin to judge. Two of the three documented 99215 claims fell below the billed level, including C0119709, a 0-condition back-pain visit documented at moderate. One claim, C0119907, was supported at high MDM with 54 minutes, and the rule check notes the pooled documentation result is not lopsided. There is no sign of cloned or inflated notes, since every note claiming moderate-or-higher data review had a matching lab or test line. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims to see whether the notes support high-complexity decision-making or 40+ minutes. This would turn a billing pattern consistent with upcoding into a documented finding, or rule it out."}
